# ObsidianUltra

> A fork of the Obsidian UI library (deividcomsono/Obsidian) for Roblox exploit scripts.
> Everything from upstream Obsidian works unchanged; this file documents only what this
> fork adds, because an LLM that knows upstream Obsidian will not know about these.

Load it the same way as upstream, but from this repo:

```lua
local repo = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/joustingmatch/ObsidianUltra/main/"
local Library = loadstring(game:HttpGet(repo .. "Library.lua"))()
```

Types for these additions live in `Library.d.luau`; `Example.lua` has runnable usage.

## Sub tabs (tabs inside a tab)

A sub tab is a second level of tabs *inside* one sidebar tab. Giving a tab sub tabs gets
you **both** views of them at once, with nothing to turn on:

- a **row of buttons** across the top of the tab's content area, above the groupboxes
- a **collapsible list** in the sidebar, indented under the tab, with a chevron to expand
  and collapse it

They are two views of the same sub tabs, not two sets. Switching in either one drives the
other, because both are painted from the same `SubTab:Show` and `SubTab:Hide`.

This is not the same thing as a **Tabbox** — a Tabbox is a small tabbed widget that lives
inside one column, while a sub tab owns the entire content area and has its own left and
right columns.

### Creating them

```lua
local Combat = Window:AddTab("Combat", "swords")

local PvP = Combat:AddSubTab("PvP")                                 -- name, icon
local Parry = Combat:AddSubTab("Parry", "shield")
local Builder = Combat:AddSubTab({ Name = "Builder", Icon = "wrench" })  -- table form
```

`Tab:AddSubTab` accepts either `(Name: string, Icon: string?)` or a
`{ Name: string, Icon: string? }` table, mirroring `Window:AddTab`. The icon is optional
and resolves through the same lucide lookup as everywhere else.

### What a sub tab supports

A sub tab is tab-like: it has its own `Sides` (left and right `ScrollingFrame`s), so every
container method a tab has works on it, and the elements inside behave identically.

```lua
PvP:AddLeftGroupbox("Aiming", "crosshair"):AddToggle("SilentAim", { Text = "Silent Aim" })
PvP:AddRightGroupbox("Targeting"):AddDropdown("HitPart", { Values = { "Head" }, Default = 1 })

local Box = Builder:AddLeftTabbox("Animation Builder")   -- tabboxes nest inside sub tabs
Box:AddTab("Timings"):AddToggle("Preview", { Text = "Preview" })
```

Available on a sub tab: `AddGroupbox`, `AddLeftGroupbox`, `AddRightGroupbox`, `AddTabbox`,
`AddLeftTabbox`, `AddRightTabbox`, `Show`, `Hide`, `SetVisible`, `Hover`, `Resize`,
`RefreshSides`, `Destroy`.

Fields: `Type` (`"SubTab"`), `Name`, `Window`, `Tab` (the parent tab), `Canvas`, `Button`,
`Sides`, `Groupboxes`, `Tabboxes`, `DependencyGroupboxes`.

### The sidebar list

A tab that has sub tabs grows a chevron on the right of its sidebar button. Clicking the
**chevron** expands or collapses the list without switching tabs; clicking the **tab
itself** switches to it and opens its list. Only one list is open at a time: opening a tab
collapses the previously open one. Selecting a nested row switches to that tab first if it
was not already open, then to the sub tab.

Every row reserves the same icon column whether or not it has an icon, so all the labels
line up. Without that, an iconless row sat further left than its siblings and read as a
level shallower in the tree.

The open sub tab's row is marked with an accent bar, an accent label, and a faint fill;
idle rows are label only at 40% transparency, and hover sits between the two. The list
animates open and closed, and the chevron rotates with it. Disable both with
`Animations = { SidebarSubTabs = false }`, which like `SubTabUnderline` defaults to `true`.

A compacted sidebar has no room for labels, so nested lists collapse while compact and the
open tab's list reopens when the sidebar expands again.

Per-tab control:

```lua
Tab:SetExpanded(true)
Tab:ToggleExpanded()
Tab:IsExpanded()
```

### The button row

The row sits above the groupboxes and reserves vertical space for itself, so tab content
starts below it. It is centered by default:

```lua
Combat:SetSubTabAlignment("Left")   -- "Left" | "Center" | "Right"
```

The active sub tab is drawn as a rounded chip: a fill lighter than `MainColor`, a thin
outline, a drop shadow, an accent label, and a bar underneath. Idle sub tabs are label only
at 40% transparency; hover sits between the two.

Hovering squashes the chip slightly (a `UIScale` tween). This applies to the active sub tab
as well — hovering the chip you are already on still responds — while every other hover
change is skipped for it.

The sub tab button is only the hit target and the layout item: it is transparent and keeps
a fixed size so the row never reflows, and everything visible sits in a scaled holder
inside it, with two offset shadow layers as siblings of the chip. Roblox renders children
above their parent, so the shadow cannot be a child of the chip it falls behind.

There is **one** underline shared by the whole bar, not one per button: it slides and
resizes to the newly active chip on every switch, gradienting from the font colour at both
ends to the accent colour in the middle. It snaps rather than slides on the first show and
when the bar is resized. Disable the slide with
`Animations = { SubTabUnderline = false }` — unlike the other animation flags it defaults
to `true`.

### Behaviour worth knowing

- **The parent tab becomes a host.** The moment a tab gets its first sub tab, that tab's
  own left/right columns are hidden. Put your groupboxes on the sub tabs, not on the
  parent tab — anything already added to the parent will disappear from view.
- The first sub tab added is shown automatically. `SubTab:Show()` switches to one;
  switching reuses the window's tab transition animation settings.
- `SubTab:SetVisible(false)` hides its button and, if it was active, falls through to
  another visible sub tab.
- Search works across sub tabs. Sub tabs whose elements do not match the query have their
  buttons hidden, and if the active sub tab has no matches the search jumps to one that
  does.
- Warning boxes still belong to the parent tab (`Tab:UpdateWarningBox`), and the sub tab
  content is offset below both the warning box and the button row.

### Related tab members

- `Tab.SubTabs` — `{ [Name]: SubTab }`
- `Tab.ActiveSubTab` — the visible sub tab, or `nil`
- `Tab:GetContentOffset()` — pixels reserved at the top of the tab by the warning box and
  the sub tab row
- `Tab:IsExpanded()`, `Tab:SetExpanded(Value?)`, `Tab:ToggleExpanded()` — the nested list
- `Library:GetActiveSides()` — the `ScrollingFrame`s currently on screen; returns the
  active sub tab's sides when there is one, otherwise the active tab's. Prefer this over
  `Library.ActiveTab.Sides`, which is wrong whenever sub tabs are in use.

## Header

The header was reworked and differs from upstream in ways that affect script authors:

- **The open tab is always named in the header.** Upstream only showed the header tab info
  when a tab was given a `Description`; here the bold tab name is always shown, with the
  description as a smaller faded second line when there is one. Give tabs a `Description`
  to fill that second line:
  `Window:AddTab({ Name = "Main", Icon = "user", Description = "Main features" })`
- `Window:ShowTabInfo(Name, Description)` accepts a `nil`/empty description and hides the
  second line instead of leaving a blank one.
- **The search box is a pill** (fully rounded, icon inset on the left, placeholder
  `"Search..."`). It is registered in `Library.PillCorners`, a third corner list added by
  this fork: those corners stay fully rounded at any corner radius above 0, and go square
  when the radius is set to 0, so the pill still obeys `Window:SetCornerRadius(0)`.
- `SearchbarSize` now defaults to `UDim2.fromScale(0.35, 1)` rather than
  `UDim2.fromScale(1, 1)`, and the box no longer resizes itself when tab info appears —
  the tab info grows to fill whatever the search box does not use. Pass your own
  `SearchbarSize` to override.

## Search v2

Header search is case insensitive and treats the query as plain text. Characters that
have meaning in a Lua pattern, such as `(`, `%`, `-`, `+`, and `[`, are searched
literally and cannot make the search error.

When the direct substring test misses, fuzzy search can match the query as a subsequence:
the same characters must appear in the same order, but other characters may sit between
them. Fuzzy matching defaults to on, only runs for queries with at least two non-whitespace
characters, and ignores whitespace in the query. Set `FuzzySearch = false` to keep only
literal substring matching.

Value search also defaults to on. In addition to an element's label, search considers:

- every dropdown entry, plus its current selection (including multi selections); a
  dropdown's `FormatListValue` is used when it has one, falling back to
  `FormatDisplayValue`, so the value is searched as it is displayed
- an input's current value
- a key picker's key name and mode, including a key picker attached to another element

At most 100 dropdown entries are checked per element on each update, so a very large list
does not stall the searchbar. Toggle and slider values, and colour picker values, are not
searched.

Container names participate too. Matching a groupbox name, a Tabbox tab name, or a nested
sub tab name shows all of that container's normally visible contents. It does not bring
back an element that the script explicitly hid.

Press **Ctrl+F** while the window is open to focus the searchbar. The shortcut does not
steal focus from another text box. While the searchbar is focused, **Escape** clears it
and releases focus. The key half of the shortcut is configurable, but Ctrl is always
required:

```lua
Library:CreateWindow({
    FuzzySearch = true,
    SearchValues = true,
    SearchKeybind = Enum.KeyCode.F,
    DisableSearchKeybind = false,
})
```

These window options set `Library.FuzzySearch` and `Library.SearchValues`; both fields can
also be changed directly. `DisableSearchKeybind = true` disables only the focus shortcut.
`DisableSearch = true` removes search and makes both keyboard behaviours no-ops.
`GlobalSearch` is separate: it still decides whether a query searches every top-level tab
or only the active one.

## Minimize

The window can collapse to a small card rather than closing. The minimize button sits in
the top right of the header, immediately left of the move icon, and the top bar reserves
room for it. This is **not** the same as sidebar compacting (`Window:SetCompact`), which
only narrows the sidebar and leaves the window at full size.

```lua
Library:CreateWindow({
    Minimizable = true,                     -- default true, removes the button when false
    MinimizeKeybind = Enum.KeyCode.RightBracket, -- optional, no default
    MinimizedWidth = 300,
    MinimizedSubtitle = "",  -- empty means "track the open tab"
})

Window:SetMinimized(true)
Window:ToggleMinimized()
Window:IsMinimized()
```

**The card needs no setup.** It is part of the window, built whenever `Minimizable` is on,
and fills itself in from what the window already knows. A script that never touches the
minimize API still gets a working card.

The card is fixed width and grows vertically to fit its contents. It has three parts:

- a **header** with the window icon in a rounded badge, the title in bold, a smaller
  subtitle beneath it, and a restore chevron on the right
- a **body** of labels, hidden entirely until the script adds one
- a **footer** showing the window footer, separated by a line

The subtitle tracks the **open tab** by default, updating as tabs are switched. Passing
`MinimizedSubtitle`, or calling `Window:SetMinimizedSubtitle`, takes it over; passing an
empty string hands it back to the automatic tab name.

The footer is the same value passed to `Footer` or `Window:SetFooter`, flattened to plain
text; the card has no room for per segment copy buttons, so a list of segments is joined
with spaces and none of it is copyable there.

Labels are the one optional part, for status worth seeing while collapsed:

```lua
local Status = Window:AddMinimizedLabel("Idle")
Status:SetText("Farming: 3 running")
Status:SetVisible(false)
Status:Destroy()

Window:SetMinimizedSubtitle("0/3 connected")
Window:SetMinimizedSubtitle("")          -- back to tracking the open tab
Window:ClearMinimizedLabels()
```

The card opens at the window's last position rather than jumping to a corner, and restoring
moves the window to wherever the card was dragged. It is dragged by its header, so the
restore button still takes clicks. The keybind is ignored while a text box has focus, and
both the card and the window stay hidden while the UI is toggled off, so minimizing never
fights `Library:Toggle`.

## Restyled toggles and sliders

These changed shape from upstream, so screenshots and pixel expectations differ. The API is
untouched — `AddToggle` and `AddSlider` take the same arguments and behave the same.

**Toggle** is a 38×20 pill. Off, the track is a grey ramp (a `UIGradient` multiplying the
track colour, landing on `#505050` → `#8A8A8A` against a white `FontColor`); on, it is the
accent colour with a gentler ramp. The ball is `FontColor` with a shadow beneath it, and
slides between the two ends.

**Slider** puts its label top left and its value top right, above a pill shaped bar, with a
ball riding the fill edge. The track is a grey ramp running light at the left to dark at
the right — the opposite direction to the switch — so the filled part always reads brighter
than the track that follows it. The filled part is the accent colour. The ball is **wider than the bar** — 18px against a 16px bar,
growing to 24px while hovered or dragged on a Sine in-out curve — so it sits proud of the
track, and the holder reserves margin for it to overflow into. It carries a shadow and a
faint outline, and the bar has an inner outline: a ring inset by a pixel, since Roblox
strokes sit outside the border and cannot be drawn inside one.

`Compact = true` sliders are unchanged: no ball, and the value stays centred in the bar,
since there is no room for the two row layout.

Buttons, sliders bars and the search box are pill shaped via `Library.PillCorners`, so they
stay fully rounded at any corner radius above 0 and square off at 0. Keybind buttons are
deliberately **not** pills: their menu attaches to the right edge and squares those corners
off while open.

## Select All / Deselect All

Multi select dropdowns get a built in row above their values with **Select All** and
**Deselect All**, in both the inline list and the expanded panel. It skips disabled values,
and while a search is typed it only touches the values matching that search.

```lua
Groupbox:AddDropdown("Materials", {
    Values = Materials,
    Multi = true,

    SelectAllButtons = true, -- default; false removes the row
})
```

Methods: `Dropdown:SelectAll(Search?)` and `Dropdown:DeselectAll(Search?)`. Both are multi
only, both fire the callback once, and `DeselectAll` keeps one value picked when
`AllowNull` is false.

## Expandable dropdowns

Every dropdown gets a small expand button beside its arrow. Clicking it opens all of the
dropdown's values in a panel over the window — a dimmed overlay with a titled panel, an
optional searchbar, and the values laid out in columns. It is the same dropdown underneath:
selecting in the panel and selecting in the inline list run identical code, and both views
stay in sync.

```lua
Groupbox:AddDropdown("Materials", {
    Values = Materials,      -- long lists are what this is for
    Multi = true,
    Searchable = true,       -- gives the panel its own searchbar

    Expandable = true,       -- default; false removes the expand button
    ExpandColumns = 3,       -- default 2
})
```

Closing: the panel's **X** button, clicking anywhere off the panel, or — when the dropdown
is single select — picking a value. Multi select panels stay open so several values can be
ticked in one visit.

Methods: `Dropdown:Expand()`, `Dropdown:Collapse()`, `Dropdown:ToggleExpanded()`,
`Dropdown:IsExpanded()`.

Notes:
- The panel's searchbar only exists when `Searchable = true`, and it is separate from the
  inline searchbar — opening the panel clears it.
- Only one dropdown can be expanded at a time; expanding one collapses another, and the
  open inline menu is closed.
- `Library.ActiveExpandedDropdown` holds the expanded dropdown, or `nil`.
- The panel is parented to `Library.MainFrame` (this fork stores the window frame there so
  elements defined outside `CreateWindow` can overlay it). If there is no window yet,
  `Expand` does nothing.
- `DisabledValues` render dimmed and unclickable in the panel, as in the inline list.

## Copyable footer

The footer is a row of segments, and each segment is either plain text or a copy target.
A copyable segment is drawn in `Library.Scheme.BlueColor` at full opacity so it reads as a
link, and gets its own small copy button; clicking the text or the button writes that
segment to the clipboard and flips the icon to a check for about 1.5 seconds. Plain
segments keep the usual 50% faded white.

### A single string

`Footer` accepts a plain string, and `CopyableFooter` (default `true`) decides whether the
whole thing is copyable:

```lua
Library:CreateWindow({
    Footer = "version: example",
    CopyableFooter = true,   -- false gives the plain grey footer
})
```

### Mixed plain and copyable text

Pass a list instead. **Bare strings are plain text**, and a table segment is only copyable
when it says `Copyable = true` — copyability is opt in per segment, and `CopyableFooter`
does not apply to this form:

```lua
Library:CreateWindow({
    Footer = {
        "version: example |",                                   -- plain
        { Text = "discord.gg/mspaint", Copyable = true },        -- blue + copy button
        "|",
        { Text = "user id", Copyable = true, CopyText = "123" }, -- copies CopyText
    },
})
```

Segment fields: `Text` (shown), `Copyable` (defaults to `false` in list form), `CopyText`
(what lands on the clipboard, defaults to `Text` — use it when the label should not be the
copied value).

Segments are laid out in a centered horizontal row with 6px between them, so put any
separators (`"|"`, `"-"`) in as their own plain segments.

### Runtime and caveats

- `Window:SetFooter(Footer)` takes either form and rebuilds the row, replacing whatever was
  there. It used to accept only a string.
- The clipboard writer is resolved once at load as
  `setclipboard or toclipboard or syn.write_clipboard`. If the executor exposes none of
  them, every segment falls back to plain text and no copy buttons are created — do not
  assume they exist.

### Scheme.BlueColor

This fork adds one scheme colour, used for the footer highlight and available to your own
elements:

- `Library.Scheme.BlueColor`, default `Color3.fromRGB(80, 155, 255)`
- Alias `"Blue"` — any property that accepts a scheme string accepts `"Blue"` or
  `"BlueColor"`, and it re-colours automatically when the theme changes
- `ThemeManager` preserves it across theme swaps, like `RedColor` and `DarkColor`
